commits.author: Jan-Hendrik Spahn
commits.message:
feat: deep link to classes, attributes, associations and enum entries; embeddable-session handshake (#252, RDFA-690)

* feat(frontend): deep-link classes, attributes, associations and enum entries

A `class` URL parameter on /mainpage (an IRI or rdfa:uuid) selects a class and
opens its package diagram; when it names an attribute, association or enum
entry instead, the declaring class opens with that row revealed and briefly
highlighted. `dataset` and `graph` narrow the lookup and either works on its
own, so `graph` alone lets an external tool open a term in the profile it
knows without having to guess what the dataset is called in this session.
Snapshot links forward these parameters after loading.

The search bar's result navigation is extracted into a shared
model-navigation helper and reused by the deep link.

Also lets an embedding host (e.g. the CIMNotebook IDE extensions) ask this
app which backend session it is using over postMessage, gated behind the
opt-in PUBLIC_EMBED_SESSION_HANDSHAKE deployment flag: datasets live in a
session, so a tool outside the browser can only read the ones you are
editing by addressing that exact session.

Enables 'Open in RDFArchitect' from the CIMNotebook IDE extensions
(SOPTIM/OpenCGMES#38).

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan-Hendrik Spahn <jan-hendrik.spahn@soptim.de>

* docs: document /mainpage deep-link URL parameters

Covers dataset/graph/package/class parameters and combining them with
snapshot links (SOPTIM/OpenCGMES#38).

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan-Hendrik Spahn <jan-hendrik.spahn@soptim.de>

* feat(backend): fall back to in-memory snapshots when Fuseki is unavailable

Snapshot creation previously hard-required a running Fuseki server, which
the default docker-compose deployment does not include. SnapshotPort gains
an isAvailable() probe (Fuseki: admin ping); PortConfig now wires a
FallbackSnapshotAdapter that prefers the persistent Fuseki store and falls
back to a new InMemorySnapshotAdapter — a process-global map of deep-copied,
UUID-stripped graphs plus the prefix mapping, shared across sessions but
lost on restart. Loaded snapshots land read-only in the session, matching
the Fuseki path.

Enables the CIMNotebook IDE extensions' snapshot-based schema handoff
against Fuseki-less deployments (SOPTIM/OpenCGMES#38).

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan-Hendrik Spahn <jan-hendrik.spahn@soptim.de>

* fix(backend): fall back to in-memory snapshots when Fuseki rejects the request

isAvailable() only probes reachability, and Fuseki's stock shiro.ini serves /$/ping
anonymously while restricting the rest of /$/** to localhost. A containerised backend
therefore got a green ping and a 403 on dataset creation, so FallbackSnapshotAdapter
chose the Fuseki path and surfaced a 500 instead of degrading.

createSnapshot and snapshotExists now treat a DatabaseException from the primary the
same as an unreachable primary and fall through to the in-memory store.

Found by running the CIMNotebook schema handoff (SOPTIM/OpenCGMES#38) against a real
Fuseki 6.1.0.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan-Hendrik Spahn <jan-hendrik.spahn@soptim.de>

* docs: document the session cookie policy for embedding RDFArchitect

A cross-site iframe host (e.g. the CIMNotebook VS Code panel) gets no session cookie
under the default same-site: lax, so the embedded app reports that no schemas were
imported. Documents same-site: none + secure: true, and notes that Secure cookies are
accepted from http://localhost.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan-Hendrik Spahn <jan-hendrik.spahn@soptim.de>

* docs: document deep-linking attributes, associations and enum entries

`class` now accepts more than classes: an attribute, association or enum
entry's IRI opens the class that declares it, with that row revealed.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan-Hendrik Spahn <jan-hendrik.spahn@soptim.de>

* feat(backend): expose the id of the current session

Datasets belong to a session, so a tool outside the browser can only work with the datasets
a user is editing if it addresses that session — and to do that it needs the session id.
Only DELETE existed on /api/session; this adds the GET that reports it.

The id is the session cookie's value, so it grants full access to the session. Whether it
may be handed to an embedding host is a separate, opt-in decision on the frontend side.

Signed-off-by: Jan-Hendrik Spahn <jan-hendrik.spahn@soptim.de>

* docs: document the embedded-session handshake opt-in

Covers the postMessage handshake an embedding host uses to learn this app's
backend session id, and the PUBLIC_EMBED_SESSION_HANDSHAKE flag that gates it.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan-Hendrik Spahn <jan-hendrik.spahn@soptim.de>

* docs: record the session handshake as a capability, not just a setting

The security page enumerates what in RDFArchitect is a bearer capability — snapshot links so
far. A session id handed to an embedding host is another, and a stronger one, so it belongs
in the same list rather than only in the configuration reference.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan-Hendrik Spahn <jan-hendrik.spahn@soptim.de>

* docs: let a deep link name the graph without the dataset

`graph` alone now narrows a `class` deep link's search, matching the code:
an external tool can say which profile a term should open in without
knowing what the dataset is called in this session.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: call a workspace a workspace where this branch says dataset

The product renamed datasets to workspaces, but the embedding docs, the
session handshake's JSDoc and `GET /api/session`'s description still
described the thing a session holds as a dataset — the wording a user
meets when reading why the handshake exists.

also still calls datasets.

Renaming the "live datasets" heading moves its anchor, so the two links
into it were updated with it. `openapi.json` is regenerated rather than
hand-edited.

commits.author: Jan-Hendrik Spahn
commits.message:
feat(import): import in the background with progress in the dialog (#243, RDFA-471)

Importing schemas used to close the dialog and do all the work in one request, with a
toast at the end as the only feedback - easy to miss, and silent for anything from 5 to
60 seconds.

The import is now a background job the dialog follows, and the part that made it slow is gone.

## Progress in the dialog

`POST .../graphs/content/imports` starts a job and answers with its id,
`GET .../imports/{jobId}` reports the progress, `DELETE .../imports/{jobId}` stops it
after the file it is currently on. Zip archives are expanded into their graph files
before anything is imported, so the counts and percentages are real, and each file
reports the step it is in (reading, checking, storing).

The dialog stays open and polls that status:

- a progress bar and one row per file — spinner while it runs, check when it is in
- files that could not be imported keep their row with the reason next to them
- properties that were stored but will not be displayed are listed in the dialog
  instead of a toast that is easy to miss
- cancelling stops after the current file and keeps the schemas that made it
- closing the dialog opens the first imported schema, as before

The synchronous `PUT .../graphs/content` is removed.

## Faster import

Importing the 11 CGMES CurrentRelease profiles took **17.0 s**, of which only 0.6 s was
parsing and storing. The rest was `createDiagramLayout`: it converted the whole graph to
a CIM collection once per package, and `insertDiagramObjectPoint` re-queries every
existing point of the diagram on each insert, which makes it quadratic in the classes of
a package.

Everything it wrote was redundant. Each point sat at (0,0), which is exactly what the
editor reads as "not laid out yet": it runs the ELK layout and persists the result
through `updateClassPositions`, which creates the diagram, diagram objects and points on
demand. So neither the import, nor replacing a graph's content, nor session start needs
to prepare them, and `CreateDiagramLayoutUseCase` with its only implementation
`UpdateDiagramLayoutService` is gone. `deletePackageLayoutData` now skips classes without
a diagram object instead of dereferencing null, and `GraphBulkImportService`, a
caller-less duplicate of `ImportGraphsService`, is removed as well.

**17.0 s → 0.6 s.** The same applies to replacing one graph's content and to every new
browser session, which used to run the layout creation for every graph of every dataset.

Signed-off-by: Jan-Hendrik Spahn <jan-hendrik.spahn@soptim.de>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Jan-Hendrik Spahn
commits.message:
fix: persist a new association into its named graph (#267, RDFA-732)

`CIMUpdates.insertAssociation` scopes its operation with `WITH <graphUri>`, but
`createAssociation` executed the request with `UpdateAction.execute(request, graph)`,
which offers the graph as the *default* graph. The insert therefore went into a named
graph nobody holds: Jena raised nothing, the transaction committed, and the API answered
with the new UUIDs, so the class editor showed the association from its optimistic store
while the diagram — which re-reads from the backend — never saw it and a reload lost it.

Both writes now go through `SessionDataStore.wrapGraphInDataset`, as `replaceAssociation`
already did; `replaceAllAssociations` had the same defect and is fixed with it.

The regression test runs on a named graph, as every schema in the app is. The existing
service tests use the "default" graph, where a missing `WITH` clause makes no difference,
which is why this went unnoticed.

Signed-off-by: Jan-Hendrik Spahn <jan-hendrik.spahn@soptim.de>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Jan-Hendrik Spahn
commits.message:
fix: profile header datatypes overwritten with entry IRIs (GH-254) (#257)

expandOntologyIris captured the entry IRI into `entryNamespace` and then
expanded that same variable again for the datatype, so every literal entry
with a datatype was stored as `"value"^^<predicateIRI>`:

    <dct:issued rdf:datatype="http://purl.org/dc/terms/issued">...

The corruption is progressive. On the first save it hits the two known
fields that carry a datatype, dct:issued (xsd:dateTime) and dct:modified
(xsd:date). From the second save on it hits every literal entry, because
OntologyFactory reports xsd:string for plain literals when the header is
read back, so the round-tripped DTO arrives with a non-null datatype that
then gets clobbered too.

Expand entry.getDatatypeIri() instead. While in the same loop, also expand
the value of IRI entries: OntologyEntryRow stores IRI values in prefixed
form just like entry IRIs and datatypes, but nothing ever expanded them,
so an IRI value under a registered namespace was written as <owl:Thing>.
Literal values stay untouched.

Adds UpdateOntologyServiceTest, which had no coverage before; all four
cases fail against the previous behaviour.

Signed-off-by: Jan-Hendrik Spahn <jan-hendrik.spahn@soptim.de>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Jan-Hendrik Spahn
commits.message:
fix: keep the diagram from freezing on an unlaid-out layout (#260, GH-256)

Every class of a diagram without a stored layout sits at (0,0), so any two of the
same measured size share a centre. getNodeIntersection had no border intersection
to compute there and turned 0 * Infinity into NaN, for the edge path and for the
placement of its labels alike.

That was fatal in syncLabelNodes, whose effect writes the nodes it reads and
compared positions with !==: NaN !== NaN reported a change on every rebuild, so
the effect never settled. Svelte aborted the batch with effect_update_depth_exceeded
and the main thread stayed busy, which left the app unresponsive and the loading
spinner up for good - the ELK layout that would have separated the classes could
no longer be delivered.

- an edge between two classes on the same spot now ends on their shared centre
- labelNodesChanged moved next to buildLabelNodes and compares coordinates with
  Object.is, so a coordinate that is not a number can no longer keep a
  self-writing effect running
- a failing ELK layout clears the loading state and says so, rather than leaving
  the user watching the spinner

Signed-off-by: Jan-Hendrik Spahn <jan-hendrik.spahn@soptim.de>

commits.author: Jan-Hendrik Spahn
commits.message:
fix: restore share snapshot (#247, RDFA-710, GH-246)

The client migration in 64d25ac1 broke every step of the snapshot flow:

- SnapshotDialog left `workspaces` undefined until the store answered, so
  opening the dialog from the File menu threw on `workspaces.length` before
  it rendered. Only the workspace tab context menu still worked, because it
  locks the workspace and hides the select.
- createSnapshot passed the workspace name as a path parameter. The endpoint
  takes it as a raw request body that the backend reads verbatim, so it has
  to be sent unserialized instead of as a quoted JSON string.
- loadSnapshot passed the token as `base64Param`, while the path placeholder
  is `base64Token`, so a shared link requested a literal
  /api/snapshots/{base64Token}.

Signed-off-by: Jan-Hendrik Spahn <jan-hendrik.spahn@soptim.de>
